title: No low-degree invariants of x-line scalar-multiplication orbits (D1)
question: D1 (speculative, from ECDLP-22): the action of scalar multiplication on x-coordinates (x ↦ x([m]Q), a degree-m² rational map on P¹ restricted to the x-values of a cyclic subgroup) admits no low-degree invariant: the least degree of a nonconstant polynomial invariant under the induced permutation of the M x-values equals M − c + 1 (c = number of cycles), as for a random permutation of the same cycle type; in particular no hidden low-degree structure is available to shortcut orbit computations.
rationale: Most promising of five new high-risk hypotheses from ECDLP-22; cheapest decisive test executed.
claims: D1 (speculative, from ECDLP-22): the action of scalar multiplication on x-coordinates (x ↦ x([m]Q), a degree-m² rational map on P¹ restricted to the x-values of a cyclic subgroup) admits no low-degree invariant: the least degree of a nonconstant polynomial invariant under the induced permutation of the M x-values equals M − c + 1 (c = number of cycles), as for a random permutation of the same cycle type; in particular no hidden low-degree structure is available to shortcut orbit computations.
next_action: Low priority: close to a theorem (any permutation-invariant polynomial has degree >= M − c + 1 when values are distinct); test has low evidential value. Other ECDLP-22 hypotheses (D2 diamond operators on X_1(r), D3 endomorphism-class speedups via Z[pi], D4 lifting/xedni (known obstruction), D5 multi-instance amortization) recorded in RUN-73ace464 as speculative backlog.
notes: Pre-registered; 50 curve/map rows, p <= 211, seed 7; PI reproduced bit-identically. Null result: matched random permutations of the same cycle type (1/150 null draws differed by 1); proved bound >= M/m^2 held.
